label: France

governmentText.minority: {party} scrapes the narrowest of wins: {seats} points.
governmentText.hung: Dead heat. France recounts through the night; the Republic holds its breath.

goalHint: Win {majority} of {total} presidency points. Six planning weeks compress the historical two-week runoff. First-round transfers are included in the opening support. National broadcasts and platform preparation reach the whole electorate.

issues.name: Pouvoir d'achat
issues.blurb: Purchasing power: the issue that decides French elections.

issues.name: Immigration & identity
issues.blurb: The far right's home turf: borders, laïcité, national identity.

issues.name: Security
issues.blurb: Crime, policing, and the sense of order.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: The retirement age, and who pays for pensions.

issues.name: Europe
issues.blurb: France's place in Europe, the single currency and who pays for it.

issues.name: Public services
issues.blurb: Hospitals, schools, and the deserted countryside.

1981.label: 1981 · Mitterrand v. Giscard
1981.tagline: May 10, 1981. Twenty-three years of the right, a second oil shock and more than a million and a half people out of work. Giscard, elected at 48, asks for a second term against the Socialist he beat by 1.6 points in 1974. Chirac's voters hold the key, and the Communists have not yet said what theirs will do.

events.headline: Mitterrand's 110 proposals promise retirement at 60, the 39-hour week and nationalisations, and {party} has a programme to run on
The Bokassa diamonds story follows the president through the campaign, and a Socialist poster of him with diamonds in his eyes keeps it alive. {party} pays
Chirac says he will vote for Giscard 'in a personal capacity' and tells no one else what to do, and part of the Gaullist vote stays home on {party}'s account
The Communist Party, at 15 percent in round one, tells its voters to beat Giscard, and the left's vote consolidates behind {party}
In the debate Mitterrand answers Giscard's old 'man of the past' refrain with 'you have become the man of the liabilities'. {party} lands the blow
Warnings of Communist ministers in a Mitterrand cabinet rally the right's base in the last week for {party}
Unemployment near a million and three quarters and inflation above 13 percent weigh on {party}
'La force tranquille' and a poster of a village church reassure rural voters, and {party} reaches the countryside
The feud between Giscard and Chirac, open since Chirac quit as prime minister in 1976, shows in every right-wing rally, and {party} pays for it

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: About 1.7 million job seekers after the second oil shock, and the left's pledge of a shorter working week.

issues.name: Inflation
issues.blurb: Prices rising more than 13 percent a year, and wage earners squeezed under Barre's austerity.

issues.name: Nationalisations
issues.blurb: The left's plan to nationalise the banks and the big industrial groups, and fear of Communist ministers.

issues.name: Sécurité et liberté
issues.blurb: Peyrefitte's 'Security and Liberty' law, and Mitterrand's pledge to abolish the death penalty.

issues.name: The diamonds affair
issues.blurb: Diamonds Giscard accepted from Bokassa of the Central African Republic as finance minister in 1973.

issues.name: Retirement at 60
issues.blurb: Mitterrand's pledge to lower the retirement age from 65 to 60.

1988.label: 1988 · Mitterrand v. Chirac
1988.tagline: May 8, 1988. Two years of cohabitation have left a Socialist president facing his own prime minister. Mitterrand runs above the parties with a letter to all the French; Chirac has a government record to defend and a rival on his own right. Le Pen's best score yet makes his voters the swing bloc.

events.headline: Mitterrand's 'Letter to all the French' and a campaign above the parties promise a 'united France', and {party} looks presidential
Le Pen takes 14.4 percent in round one, a record for the Front National, and {party} courts his voters without striking a deal
Barre, eliminated, backs Chirac without warmth, and the centre's voters stay unsure about {party}
In the debate Chirac says they are equal candidates, and Mitterrand answers 'you are quite right, Prime Minister'. The line sticks to {party}
The last French hostages in Lebanon come home days before the vote, and {party}'s government takes the credit
The assault on the Ouvéa cave in New Caledonia ends in 21 deaths three days before the vote, and the questions land on {party}
Two years of cohabitation leave voters tired of the quarrel, and they reward the president who stayed above it, {party}
The Communist vote falls to 6.8 percent in round one, its worst score ever, and its voters line up behind {party} for the runoff
The privatisation programme and the 1987 stock market crash leave small savers angry, and {party} carries the bill

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: About one worker in ten is out of a job, and both finalists promise to bring the number down.

issues.name: Terrorism & hostages
issues.blurb: The 1986 Paris bombings, the Lebanon hostages freed on May 4 and the Ouvéa cave assault.

issues.name: Immigration & nationality
issues.blurb: The 1986 Pasqua law, the shelved reform of the nationality code and Le Pen's 14.4 percent.

issues.name: Privatisations
issues.blurb: Chirac's sell-off of Saint-Gobain, Paribas and TF1, and small shareholders' losses in the October crash.

issues.name: Education
issues.blurb: Mitterrand makes schools his priority, after the 1986 student protests that sank the Devaquet bill.

issues.name: Wealth tax & minimum income
issues.blurb: Mitterrand's plan to bring back a wealth tax, abolished in 1986, to fund a guaranteed minimum income.

issues.name: The 1992 single market
issues.blurb: The Single European Act and the deadline to open the internal market by the end of 1992.

1995.label: 1995 · Chirac v. Jospin
1995.tagline: May 7, 1995. Mitterrand is leaving after fourteen years. The right split between Chirac and his own prime minister Balladur, and the Socialist Jospin topped round one with a party that expected to lose. Chirac, on his third try, promises to heal the 'social fracture'. Jospin promises to keep what worked under Mitterrand and drop the rest.

events.headline: Jospin tops round one at 23.3 percent. The Socialists' surprise opens a real contest, and {party} has momentum it did not expect
Balladur, eliminated in round one, backs Chirac, and the right closes ranks behind {party}
Chirac's 'social fracture' theme wins workers and young voters the right had not reached, and {party} gains
Jospin's 'right of inventory' on the Mitterrand years annoys the party's loyalists and reassures independents. {party} gains in the centre
A courteous debate with little tension. The line that lingers is Jospin's 'better five years with Jospin than seven with Chirac', and {party} still needs a swing
Le Pen, fourth with 15 percent, refuses to endorse either finalist, and much of his vote drifts to {party} or stays home
A third run for the presidency: Chirac has lost before, and a campaign built on 'now or never' energises {party}
Unemployment above three million and fatigue after fourteen years of Mitterrand weigh on {party}
The bitter first-round fight with Balladur leaves some of the right cool on Chirac, and some of its vote may stay home. A drag on {party}

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: More than three million job seekers, and every candidate claims a plan to bring the number down.

issues.name: Fracture sociale
issues.blurb: Chirac's theme of exclusion: the homeless, the long-term unemployed and estates cut off from the rest.

issues.name: Wages
issues.blurb: Chirac says the pay slip is not the enemy of jobs, against the wage restraint of recent years.

issues.name: Crime & the suburbs
issues.blurb: Crime and unrest on the housing estates, and Pasqua's tough line at the interior ministry.

issues.name: Maastricht & the currency
issues.blurb: Meeting the Maastricht deficit rules on the road to a single European currency by 1999.

issues.name: Les affaires
issues.blurb: Corruption cases that forced three of Balladur's ministers to resign in 1994.

issues.name: Immigration
issues.blurb: The 1993 Pasqua laws on entry and nationality, and Le Pen's 15 percent in round one.

2002.label: 2002 · Chirac v. Le Pen
2002.tagline: May 5, 2002. On April 21 Prime Minister Jospin finished third and was out, and for the first time a candidate of the Front National stands in a presidential runoff. Jean-Marie Le Pen's party wants sharply lower immigration and priority for French citizens in jobs and housing. Two weeks of street protest, a president who has to win big, and a vote that will not feel like a normal election.

events.headline: Le Pen takes second place in round one, about 200,000 votes ahead of the prime minister, and the country wakes up to a runoff nobody planned for
Protests against Le Pen fill the streets of every large city, school students lead them, and {party} is the beneficiary of the front républicain
Jospin retires from politics on election night. The Socialists, Greens and Communists tell their voters to back Chirac, and {party} gains the left's votes
Chirac refuses a televised debate with Le Pen, and the challenger's campaign is left without its big stage. A hit to {party}
May Day brings well over a million people into the streets against Le Pen, and the Front National answers with its Joan of Arc parade, a test of {party}'s turnout
Polls give Chirac a huge lead and his team fears complacency. A last push to turn out, and {party} has to keep a landslide from becoming an abstention story
Banners read 'vote for the crook, not the fascist' as left-wing voters hold their noses. The win comes with less warmth for {party}
Crime reports have led the news for weeks, and the debate stays on the ground where {party} is strongest

issues.name: Insécurité
issues.blurb: Crime figures on the news every night and the beating of Paul Voise in Orléans days before round one.

issues.name: Front républicain
issues.blurb: Whether left-wing voters back Chirac to block the Front National after the April 21 shock.

issues.name: National preference
issues.blurb: Le Pen's priority for French citizens in jobs, housing and benefits, and an end to immigration.

issues.name: Jobs & the 35 hours
issues.blurb: Unemployment has stopped falling, and the 35-hour week divides employers and workers.

issues.name: Tax cuts
issues.blurb: Chirac's pledge to cut income tax by a third over five years.

issues.name: Europe & the euro
issues.blurb: Le Pen wants France out of the euro, whose coins and notes arrived in January, and back to the franc.

2007.label: 2007 · Sarkozy v. Royal
2007.tagline: May 6, 2007. A former interior minister who promises a break with twelve years of Chirac against the first woman to reach a presidential runoff. Bayrou's eighteen percent has no home, Le Pen's voters are being courted openly, and one debate is the only head-to-head of the campaign.

events.headline: Sarkozy tops round one by five points, and {party} needs nearly every Bayrou and left-wing voter to catch him
Sarkozy's March pledge of a Ministry of Immigration and National Identity keeps Le Pen voters in his column, and {party} collects them
Bayrou says he will not vote for Sarkozy and talks with Royal in public. He endorses no one, but part of his vote moves to {party}
'Work more to earn more': the tax-free overtime pledge fills halls in factory towns for {party}
In the entre-deux-tours debate Royal's flash of anger over disabled children's schooling lets Sarkozy play the calm one, and {party} pays
Royal warns on the final Friday that a Sarkozy win risks violence and brutality, and {party} brings out the left's last reserves
The memory of March's Gare du Nord riot after a ticket check keeps security on the front pages, and the ground favours {party}
Royal's off-script remarks on trips abroad earlier in the campaign and the Socialist party's quarrels dent {party}'s image of competence

issues.name: Pouvoir d'achat
issues.blurb: Wages squeezed since the euro: Sarkozy offers tax-free overtime and Royal a 1,500 euro minimum wage.

issues.name: Security
issues.blurb: Sarkozy's record at the interior ministry, the 2005 suburban riots and the Gare du Nord clash in March.

issues.name: Work & the 35 hours
issues.blurb: 'Work more to earn more' against the 35-hour week, with unemployment above 8 percent.

issues.name: Identité nationale
issues.blurb: Sarkozy's planned ministry of immigration and national identity, and 'chosen' rather than 'endured' immigration.

issues.name: Civil service
issues.blurb: Sarkozy's pledge to replace only one in two retiring civil servants, against Royal's defence of public services.

issues.name: Europe after the No
issues.blurb: Reviving Europe after the 2005 No: Sarkozy's mini-treaty through parliament or Royal's new referendum.

issues.name: Public debt
issues.blurb: Bayrou made the national debt his theme, and both finalists now court his 18.6 percent.

issues.name: Special pension schemes
issues.blurb: Sarkozy's plan to bring rail and energy workers' special pension schemes into line with the general regime.

2012.label: 2012 · Hollande v. Sarkozy
2012.tagline: May 6, 2012. A one-term incumbent nobody warmed to against a Socialist who promised to be normal. 'Le changement, c'est maintenant' against a crisis president. Two weeks, and a narrow win either way.

events.headline: The euro crisis is the backdrop to everything: austerity, unemployment past three million, and {party} owns five years of it
The Toulouse and Montauban killings freeze the campaign, and the security-and-identity ground briefly favours the incumbent's {party}
'Moi, président de la République': the 'normal president' anaphora lands the debate for {party}
'Ni Sarkozy': after a record far-right first round, Le Pen's voters won't be told where to go, and the right finalist's {party} can't bank them all
'Le changement, c'est maintenant': ten years of rejection of the sitting president crystallize behind {party}
Bayrou announces he will vote Hollande, and the centre's blessing nudges wavering moderates toward {party}
A May Day rally at the Trocadéro and a hard pivot to the right rally the incumbent's {party} base in the final days

issues.name: Pouvoir d'achat
issues.blurb: Record fuel prices and the 'social VAT' rise voted in February to take effect in October.

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: Unemployment near 10 percent and plant closures such as the idle Florange blast furnaces.

issues.name: Euro crisis & the treaty
issues.blurb: Hollande would renegotiate the European fiscal treaty that Sarkozy and Merkel pushed through in March.

issues.name: Taxing the rich
issues.blurb: Hollande's 75 percent rate on incomes above one million euros, after France lost its AAA rating.

issues.name: Schools & civil service
issues.blurb: Hollande's 60,000 new posts in education, against Sarkozy's one-in-two rule for retiring civil servants.

issues.name: Retirement at 60
issues.blurb: Hollande would restore retirement at 60 for those who started work at 18, undoing part of the 2010 reform.

issues.name: Security
issues.blurb: The Toulouse and Montauban killings in March, and Sarkozy's record on crime since 2002.

issues.name: Immigration
issues.blurb: Sarkozy's pledge to halve legal immigration, and the row over halal meat started by Le Pen.

2017.label: 2017 · The Front Républicain
2017.tagline: May 7, 2017. A 39-year-old insurgent with a startup for a party against the FN's first runoff since 2002. The dam holds everywhere. The only question is by how much.

events.headline: The Whirlpool car park: Le Pen's selfies against Macron's hour in the crowd. Both camps claim Amiens
The front républicain holds its nose and rallies: 'contre l'extrême droite', and so, for Macron
'En Marche!' Obama's endorsement video hands the insurgent a global-stage glow
Debate meltdown: an aggressive, fact-free entre-deux-tours. Le Pen loses the presidency on live TV
#MacronLeaks dumps 36 hours before the vote. The campaign blackout blunts it, the doubt lingers
'Ni-ni': Mélenchon won't say the name, and the abstention question gnaws at the centre's margin
Le Pen steps 'above the party' for the runoff, and the de-demonized Marine plays presidential for a news cycle
Deindustrialized France seethes: shuttered factories put pouvoir d'achat on the RN's side of the ledger

issues.name: Europe & the euro
issues.blurb: Le Pen's plan to leave the euro and hold a referendum on the EU, against Macron's pro-European line.

issues.name: Immigration & identity
issues.blurb: Le Pen's moratorium on legal immigration and an end to citizenship by birth on French soil.

issues.name: Terrorism
issues.blurb: More than 230 killed in attacks since 2015, the state of emergency and the Champs-Élysées shooting in April.

issues.name: Unemployment & labour law
issues.blurb: Unemployment near 10 percent, the 2016 labour law protests and Macron's plan to reform by decree.

issues.name: Pouvoir d'achat
issues.blurb: Low wages in left-behind towns, and Macron's pledge to scrap the housing tax for most households.

issues.name: Mondialisation
issues.blurb: The Whirlpool plant in Amiens moving to Poland, and an open France against a protected one.

issues.name: Civil service cuts
issues.blurb: Macron's plan to cut 120,000 public posts, and Le Pen's promise to protect local services.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: Le Pen would bring back retirement at 60, and Macron plans a single points-based system.

2022.label: 2022 · Macron v. Le Pen
2022.tagline: April 24, 2022. The rematch nobody wanted twice: pouvoir d'achat against l'État McKinsey, war on the continent, and a much better-drilled Le Pen. Two weeks to hold the Republic's line.

events.headline: The McKinsey affair: millions in consulting fees, zero corporate tax. 'l'État McKinsey' sticks to the incumbent
Retraite à 65 ans: the pension line detonates on the left, and Macron's own reform becomes the attack ad
One theme, hammered daily: Le Pen's pouvoir d'achat campaign owns the caddie and the fuel pump
The Putin handshake photo, brandished on set: the Russian bank loan. 'Vous dépendez du pouvoir russe'
A calmer entre-deux-tours: Le Pen survives the rematch, but loses it on points
'Élisez-moi Premier ministre': Mélenchon reframes the runoff as round one of a troisième tour, deflating {party}
Pump prices spike again. Every full tank is a Le Pen leaflet, and the incumbent owns the price board
Split-screen politics: McKinsey invoices against the supermarket caddie. The cost-of-living contrast lands for the RN
War on the continent: Kyiv calls the Élysée and the commander-in-chief effect kicks in for the centre

issues.name: Pouvoir d'achat
issues.blurb: Fuel and food prices up since the war began, and Le Pen's plan to cut VAT on energy to 5.5 percent.

issues.name: Retirement at 65
issues.blurb: Macron's plan to raise the retirement age to 65, against Le Pen's 60 to 62 depending on career.

issues.name: Immigration & the veil
issues.blurb: Le Pen's referendum on immigration and her plan to ban the Muslim headscarf in public places.

issues.name: Ukraine & Europe
issues.blurb: Russia's invasion of Ukraine, her party's 2014 loan from a Russian bank and her plans for the EU.

issues.name: Security
issues.blurb: Police numbers, crime in the suburbs and Le Pen's 'presumption of self-defence' for police officers.

issues.name: Hospitals & schools
issues.blurb: Hospitals worn down by two years of COVID, closed beds and low pay for teachers.

issues.name: The McKinsey affair
issues.blurb: A Senate report on a billion euros of state consulting in 2021 and McKinsey paying no French profits tax.

issues.name: Écologie
issues.blurb: Macron's promise of 'ecological planning' to win left voters, and Le Pen's halt to new wind farms.

2027.label: 2027 · The Republic's Runoff
2027.tagline: April 2027. Macron is term-limited, the first round is done, and for the first time the RN enters a runoff at parity. Two weeks. Every point counts.

events.headline: The post-Macron succession scramble spills into the open as the centre squabbles over its own crown
Normalization pays: prime-time profiles cast the RN as a party of government, suits and spreadsheets
A ratings agency downgrades French debt, and the bill for the Macron years lands on the centre's doorstep
Cohabitation dread: markets and Brussels game out an RN Élysée, and hesitant voters flinch
One more time with feeling: the front républicain question. Eliminated candidates' voters break, reluctantly, for the centre
A banlieue security flashpoint drags the final days onto the RN's ground

issues.name: Pouvoir d'achat
issues.blurb: Wages, energy bills and rents after the price rises of 2022 and 2023.

issues.name: Immigration
issues.blurb: The RN's planned referendum on immigration and national priority in jobs, housing and benefits.

issues.name: Debt & deficit
issues.blurb: A deficit near 6 percent of GDP, credit downgrades and governments that fell over their budgets.

issues.name: Security
issues.blurb: Drug-trafficking violence spreading from Marseille to smaller towns, and police numbers.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: Whether to keep, pause or repeal the 2023 reform that raised the retirement age to 64.

issues.name: Public services
issues.blurb: Overstretched hospital emergency rooms, rural areas without doctors and schools short of teachers.

issues.name: Europe & Ukraine
issues.blurb: Aid to Ukraine, European defence spending and how far the RN would push back against Brussels.

events.headline: {party}'s candidate wins the entre-deux-tours debate
The front républicain stirs, and eliminated candidates' voters break for {party}
A dérapage: an ugly remark from a {party} surrogate dominates the cycle
A fuel-price spike lands hardest on {party}
A security incident pushes the campaign onto {party}'s ground
Abstention warnings mobilize {party}'s ground game
A wave of editorials rallies to {party}
A packed stadium meeting electrifies {party}
The networks offer {party} a debate slot
events.prompt: A head-to-head is on the table. How do you play it?

choices.text: Accept and go on the attack
choices.resultText: You land blows and take a few. The overnight polls twitch your way.
A steady, on-message night. No gaffes, no fireworks.

choices.text: Decline: protect the lead, avoid the ambush
choices.resultText: You dodge the studio lights. The press calls it caution.

events.headline: {party} must decide how hard to lean on the front républicain
events.prompt: The runoff arithmetic is everything. What's the play?

choices.text: Court the centre: soft tone, broad tent
choices.resultText: Moderates warm up. Your base yawns.

choices.text: Base first: turn out your own
choices.resultText: The faithful roar. The centre looks away.

choices.text: Make it a contrast night against the rival
choices.resultText: You define them, and it lands.

events.headline: {party}'s programme committee is split on the big pledge
events.prompt: The draft is ready. Which way do you push?

choices.text: Go bold with a defining, risky pledge
choices.resultText: The base roars. The spreadsheets at HQ look nervous.

choices.text: Play it cautious: no hostages to fortune
Make it a contrast document against the rival
choices.resultText: You define them more than yourself, and it lands.
